rounds.q: How many little colored squares are on a classic twisty puzzle cube?
rounds.why: Six sides of nine squares each, all riding on just 26 small cubes around a hidden center.
rounds.fun: Six sides, nine squares each, 54 in all. And only 26 small cubes doing the work!

rounds.q: What year did the first teddy bear go on sale?
rounds.why: The first ones were sewn by a couple who ran a candy store in Brooklyn.
rounds.src: History.com, First teddy bear goes on sale (Feb. 15, 1903). National Park Service, The Story of the Teddy Bear
rounds.fun: Teddy has been on sale since 1903, starting out at a candy store in Brooklyn.

rounds.q: How many cents did the very first box of 8 crayons cost?
rounds.why: That first box went on sale in 1903, and one nickel bought all eight crayons.
rounds.fun: One nickel for eight crayons back in 1903. What a colorful bargain!

rounds.q: How many pounds can one small plastic building brick hold before it's crushed?
rounds.why: It would take a stack of 375,000 bricks, over 2 miles tall, to crush the bottom one.
rounds.src: BBC News Magazine, How tall can a Lego tower get? (Open University test of 2x2 bricks, 2012)
rounds.fun: One small brick holds 950 pounds. You would need a stack over 2 miles tall to crush it!

rounds.q: How many feet of wire are coiled into one classic stair-walking spring toy?
rounds.why: The original from 1945 wound all that wire into 98 coils and sold for just $1.
rounds.src: PBS American Experience, Slinky. The Strong National Toy Hall of Fame, Slinky
rounds.fun: About 80 feet of wire in 98 coils, all for $1. That is a long walk down the stairs!
